ocr.notes: Matches the image closely (image reads 'Porkopolis', 'Frence Nation' typo in print). Transcript ends where the clipping ends, so the benefit section is missing.

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Evening Dispatch reprinted a Cincinnati Gazette report that Allen was released on $3,000 bail at Covington after the Goss fight, and that he accused referee Eph Holland of dishonesty.

metadata.notes: Masthead reads 'St. Louis Dispatch, Wednesday Evening, September 13, 1876'. Before 1878-12, so filed as the St. Louis Evening Dispatch, not the Post-Dispatch. Item is reprinted 'From the Cincinnati Gazette of Yesterday' (Sept. 12).

facts.fact: After the Goss fight Allen was released from custody in Covington, Kentucky, when Judge Perkins of the Kenton Criminal Court reduced his bail to $3,000 on a writ of habeas corpus
On his release Allen left Covington for Cincinnati, where crowds followed him through the streets
Allen said he had put up his own stake money and now believed referee Eph Holland had used it against him, and claimed that in a fair fight he could have whipped Goss in half an hour
A benefit for Allen was announced at Robinson's Opera-House in Cincinnati

notes: Release date taken as the day before the Gazette of Sept. 12 ('yesterday morning'). The benefit fact comes only from the headline; the section describing it is outside the clipping. Allen's statements are reported speech, not verbatim quotes.
